newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain key rate could fall below 5 pct - Tokai.
newsitem.headline: Spain key rate could fall below 5 pct - Tokai.

text.p: Spain's key money market rate will fall below five percent only after Spain has secured a spot in the group of nations launching the euro, Tokai bank said in its latest report on the Spanish economy.

"Realistically this could happen in the autumn," it said. "If EMU goes ahead on time and Spain does participate, domestic monetary policy throught next year will also be geared to a smooth convergence of short rates on levels prevailing in the core countries."
The Bank of Spain's key money market rate stands at 5.25 percent.
But until European convergence conditions prevail over domestic issues, sticky inflation will keep the Bank of Spain from changing the rate, the report said.

"The sharp fall in Spanish inflation of late has come to an end. With favourable food price developments now petering out, keeping inflation below two percent in line with the Bank of Spain's target for the next year will mean making inroads into structural elements of Spanish inflation."
"The target will prove particularly difficult if services inflation, which accounts for 30.6 percent of CPI, fails to fall through the 3.0 percent barrier".
June CPI rose 1.6 percent year on year versus May's 1.5 percent.
